subject: Isolated workload rightsizing playbook for Acme Health — hosting posture options
messages:
From: Elena Marks <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting posture — initial CPU/GPU ask and compliance timeline

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We need a concise recommendation from Redwood to include in our procurement packet: a scoped comparison between a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) and a Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment for our regulated clinical workflows. Key asks from procurement:

- Rough GPU count and node footprint for a 1M request/month clinical pipeline (batch + real-time mix).
- Expected 99th pct latency envelope for the real-time path (95% confidence).
- Incremental costs and contract term assumptions for private hosting (one-time setup, monthly infra).
- What security artifacts you can provide up-front (SOC2, network segmentation designs, KMS integration notes).
- A recommended path for a 6-week pilot to validate latency and audit controls.

We'd like a short write-up + an estimate by EOD today if possible to feed into our RFP.

Best,
Elena
Elena Marks
Director, Clinical AI Programs
Acme Health

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marks <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting posture — initial CPU/GPU ask and compliance timeline

Elena,

Appreciate the clear list — we can definitely get you a compact recommendation for procurement. High level first pass here (I asked Marissa to pull numbers + a worksheet; sending the detailed calc next):

Option A — Dedicated (Reserved GPU pool):
- Footprint: 8x A100-80GB or equivalent per 1M monthly mix (approx 6k rps*peak burst shaping; continuous batching assumed).
- 99th pct latency (real-time path): ~220-350 ms depending on model choices + batching config.
- Commercial: usage-based + reserved baseline (monthly committed). Lower onboarding time; no infra/legal integration required on your side.

Option B — Private (VPC / customer-managed):
- Footprint: 6–10 GPUs (A100/RTX-class) depending on redundancy & compliance requirements; one-time integration for networking and KMS.
- 99th pct latency: ~160-300 ms if co-located in customer VPC (networking dependent).
- Commercial: platform subscription + optional professional services for hardened deployment and audit support. Higher one-time setup and longer contracting.

I'll let Marissa drop the spreadsheet with specific cost rows, contract term assumptions, and the pilot plan. Also looping Lauren for legal/controls sign-off language we can hand to procurement.

If it's urgent for your packet, Marissa, can you send the worksheet and a recommended single-line ask (preferred option + fallback) that Elena can paste into the RFP?

- Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marks <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting posture — initial CPU/GPU ask and compliance timeline

Elena / team — attaching a short worksheet (acme_capacity_calc_v2.xlsx) and my recommended language for your RFP. Quick summary up-front, then numbers: 

Executive recommendation (one-liner you can paste):
"Redwood recommends an initial Dedicated reserved GPU pool for a 6-week pilot (8x A100-80GB equivalent, committed baseline) with a conditional transition to a Private VPC-managed deployment post-SOC2 evidence review and network validation. This approach minimizes time-to-value while preserving a path to isolated tenancy for long-term compliance"

Sizing & cost (high-level):
- Workload mix used: 70% async batch (offline scoring), 30% low-latency clinical inference (chat-like flows + structured output).
- Synthetic perf assumptions: using rMPT-7b-like throughput and a small set of perf-optimized kernels.

Estimated compute footprint: (numbers are rounded)
- Dedicated baseline: 8 GPUs (A100-80GB) + 2 warm spare nodes for maintenance => 10 nodes total.
- Private baseline: 6 GPUs (if colocated and customer provides networking) + 2 redundancy => 8 nodes, but add ~20% for isolation overhead (8 * 1.2 => ~10 effective nodes for procurement).

Cost model (monthly, USD):
- Dedicated reserved: $67,000 / month (committed baseline pricing assumption; includes runtime + support).
- Private hosting (redwood-managed control plane, customer infra): $92,000 / month + one-time integration fee $45,000 (network, KMS, audit runbook).
- Pilot (6 weeks, Dedicated): $35,000 flat (pro-rated commit + pilot engineering + observability retention).

Latency expectations (99th pct for real-time path):
- Dedicated: 220–350ms (depends on quantization, model size; we can tune batching to push lower for critical flows).
- Private: 160–300ms if colocated and with optimized network path; we conservatively assume ~10–20% increased tail when cross-VPC or transit gateways are involved.

Security artifacts available immediately: SOC2 Type II summary report, network zoning diagrams, our data flow diagram (DFD), KMS integration patterns. I attached a scoped evidence bundle (soc2_scoped_evidence.pdf) for initial review — procurement will want the full evidentiary package during legal diligence.

Pilot plan (6 weeks):
Week 0–1: Onboard dedicated pool, baseline perf tests with your pre-prod data sample.
Week 2–3: Run inference load tests; measure latency P50/P95/P99 against target SLAs.
Week 4: Compliance smoke test (audit checklist items; encryption at rest/in transit verification).
Week 5: Failure/DR simulation and fallback exercise.
Week 6: Operational review; decision point — continue on Dedicated vs plan migration to Private.

Notes on procurement asks:
- Contract term: Dedicated pilot followed by a 12–24 month committed baseline for best economics.
- For Private, expect 60–90 day procurement/engineering window for full network hardening.

Attachments: acme_capacity_calc_v2.xlsx, soc2_scoped_evidence.pdf, legal_routing_memo.txt

If you want I can convert the spreadsheet into a single-slide PDF for procurement to paste into the packet.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Marks <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting posture — initial CPU/GPU ask and compliance timeline

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick follow-ups from procurement before we seed the RFP: 

- Can Redwood confirm whether the SOC2 docs include encryption key management details (specifically HSM vs KMS flows)?
- For the Private option, does Redwood require a minimum committed term for the managed control plane, or can we run a month-to-month subscription while we complete legal?
- In the Dedicated numbers, is there a recommended buffer for usage spikes beyond the 10% spare? Our legal ops is worried about a clinical surge scenario.

If you can answer inline that will save us a call. We may also need a short statement from Redwood legal on data residency constraints for backups (we prefer backups in our AWS account).

Thanks — I need the answers by EOD tomorrow to include in our package.

Subject: Re: Hosting posture — initial CPU/GPU ask and compliance timeline

Elena — quick note from leadership:

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. Two pragmatic clarifications from our side that I recommend you paste into procurement to reduce back-and-forth: 

1) SOC2 / KMS: Our SOC2 package includes mapping to our key management approach; for customers who require an HSM-backed key store in their account we support either (a) Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) with KMS/HSM in the customer AWS account or (b) Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys (we can provide architecture and attestation). We'll mark which controls map to which artifacts in the evidence bundle.

2) Committed terms & buffer: For the Dedicated pilot we recommend a pro-rated 6-week pilot (no long-term commitment). Post-pilot we normally convert to a 12-month committed baseline for the economics shown. For surge protection: we recommend a staged buffer policy — reserve 10% baseline capacity + an on-call burst pool (price-at-use) sized at 30% that can be spun up within minutes. That keeps procurement from over-committing while giving clinical ops a fallback for surges.

If it helps, we can provide a short legal statement around backup residency ("customer backups stored in customer AWS account by default"), and we'll include a standard addendum for backup residency and key ownership.

Happy to join a 20-minute procurement sync tomorrow if you want to close the packet.

—Vivek
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
